checks_performed: Read only the specified source input and draft; used no web access or other source files.
Compared the exact target with the draft’s headline, final writeup, and all eleven claims.
Reconstructed the planar-duality, face-counting, induced-forest, CAI, suppression, and quadrilateral-switch arguments independently.

Exhaustively checked all 512 bipartite 3-by-3 adjacency matrices for claim 9 using integer and Boolean operations; exactly K3,3 and its nine one-edge deletions satisfy the required deletion condition.

Enumerated all exact integer face profiles for half-orders 2 through 15 for claim 10; the checker found no counterexample profile through m=12 or at m=14, one profile at m=13, and nine at m=15, with every m=13 or m=15 profile having the two required hexagon-only classes.

claims.claim: The planar dual T of G is a simple Eulerian plane triangulation with a proper vertex 3-colouring I1,I2,I3, unique up to permuting the colours.
claims.evidence: A 3-connected planar graph has a polyhedral embedding, so its dual has neither loops nor parallel edges. Cubicity makes every dual face triangular, while bipartiteness makes every primal facial cycle even and hence every dual degree even. Assigning three colours to one triangle and propagating across adjacent triangles is consistent around each vertex because its degree is even; once the initial triangle is coloured, every subsequent colour is forced. Thus the colouring exists and is unique up to the initial permutation.

claims.claim: For each colour i, the boundaries of the primal faces corresponding to Ii are pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles covering V(G). Moreover, each colour class has total face perimeter n=|V(G)|, G has n/2+2 faces, and it has at least six quadrilateral faces.
claims.evidence: The three faces incident with any primal vertex correspond to one triangular face of T and therefore have distinct colours. Consequently exactly one face of each colour contains each primal vertex, proving disjointness, coverage, and perimeter n. Cubicity gives |E|=3n/2, so Euler’s formula gives |F|=n/2+2. Finally, sum_f(6-|f|)=6|F|-2|E|=12. All facial lengths are even and at least four; quadrilaterals contribute 2 and longer faces contribute at most zero, so at least six quadrilaterals are necessary.
claims.search_method: Direct incidence counting and Euler arithmetic.

claims.claim: G is Hamiltonian if and only if V(T) can be partitioned into two sets inducing forests.
claims.evidence: For a partition X,Y into induced forests, every triangular face has exactly two cross edges. If N=|V(T)|, this gives 2N-4 cross edges and N-2 internal edges. The two forests therefore have two components in total and hence are both trees. The primal edges dual to the cross edges form a spanning 2-factor. Its components separate the sphere into regions corresponding exactly to components of the internal dual graph; the two dual trees give two regions, so the factor has one cycle. Conversely, a Hamiltonian cycle separates the primal faces into two connected sets. The n/2 noncycle edges are precisely their internal dual edges, totaling N-2; connectedness then forces both induced dual subgraphs to be trees.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional planar-duality proof with exact edge and component counts.

claims.claim: If any bichromatic graph H=T[Ii union Ij] has a CAI-partition, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: Let A union J be the CAI-partition and Ik the omitted colour. T[A] is a tree. If T[J union Ik] contained a cycle, connectedness of A would place A wholly on one side of that Jordan curve. The triangulated region on the other side would then contain a triangular face entirely in J union Ik, impossible because J and Ik are each independent. Thus J union Ik induces a forest, and claim 2 yields a Hamiltonian cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct CAI extension and Jordan-curve argument.

claims.claim: In particular, G is Hamiltonian whenever some bichromatic graph T[Ii union Ij] is series-parallel.
claims.evidence: Every bichromatic graph here is simple and 2-vertex-connected. The supplied source proves that every simple 2-connected series-parallel graph admits a CAI-partition: a short nested ear decomposition exists, and processing its ears while placing at most one suitable vertex per ear in the independent set makes the complement grow only by induced pendant paths, preserving a tree. Claim 3 then applies.
claims.search_method: Checked the source’s short nested-ear proof and the reduction through claim 3.

claims.claim: For distinct colours i,j, let Qij have the i-coloured faces as vertices, with one edge for every j-coloured quadrilateral joining the two i-coloured faces opposite it. Then G has a spanning 2-factor with exactly c(Qij) cycles. In particular, connected Qij certifies Hamiltonicity.
claims.evidence: Begin with the facial 2-factor from colour i. On each relevant quadrilateral its boundary edges alternate between belonging and not belonging to this factor, and its two incident i-faces are distinct because T is simple. Choose a spanning forest of Qij and toggle the four boundary edges for each selected quadrilateral. Same-coloured quadrilaterals are vertex-disjoint, so toggles do not interfere. Each forest edge joins two currently distinct factor cycles and its toggle merges them. Starting with |V(Qij)| cycles and performing |V(Qij)|-c(Qij) merges leaves exactly c(Qij) cycles.
claims.search_method: Constructive symmetric-difference proof with a spanning forest of Qij.

claims.claim: Every target graph on n vertices has a spanning 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.
claims.evidence: Let a be the smallest face-colour-class size. Since there are n/2+2 faces, a is at most floor((n+4)/6). If a=1, its facial boundary is Hamiltonian; target graphs have n>=8, so the asserted bound is at least one. If a>=2, at least one other colour contains a quadrilateral: otherwise both other classes, and hence the minimal class as well, would have at most n/6 faces, contradicting the total n/2+2. That quadrilateral supplies a nonloop edge of the corresponding Qij, so c(Qij)<=a-1. Claim 5 supplies the required 2-factor.
claims.search_method: Exact face-count bound combined with the quadrilateral-switch construction.

claims.claim: Let H be 2-vertex-connected. Suppress its maximal degree-2 paths to a multigraph K, let B be the vertices of degree at least three, and let U=H[B], the unsubdivided skeleton edges. If U is a forest, or U-v is a forest for some v in B, then H has a CAI-partition.
claims.evidence: If H is a cycle, one vertex forms the independent set and the rest form a path. Otherwise, extend U to a spanning tree of K, or put v in the independent set and extend U-v to a spanning tree of connected K-v. Every non-tree skeleton edge not incident with v must be subdivided; choose one internal vertex from each such path for the independent set. These vertices lie on distinct maximal degree-2 paths and are nonadjacent, and none is adjacent to v. The intact tree paths form a subdivided tree, while every cut non-tree path and every path formerly incident with v leaves only pendant fragments. Hence the complement is an induced tree.
claims.search_method: Complete constructive proof, including cycle and deleted-skeleton-vertex cases.

claims.claim: In any counterexample, every face-colour class contains at least three nonquadrilateral faces; for every colour pair, their nonquadrilateral-face adjacency graph has feedback-vertex number at least two. Moreover, every Qij is disconnected and every bichromatic graph is non-series-parallel.
claims.evidence: In a bichromatic graph, a face of perimeter l has degree l/2, so its degree-at-least-three vertices are exactly the nonquadrilateral faces and their induced adjacency graph is U from claim 7. In a counterexample U cannot become a forest after deleting at most one vertex, so its feedback-vertex number is at least two. If one bipartition side contained at most two such vertices, U would already be acyclic or would become acyclic after deleting one of them; hence every colour class contains at least three. Connected Qij and series-parallel bichromatic graphs are excluded respectively by claims 5 and 4.
claims.search_method: Contrapositive application of claims 4, 5, and 7 with degree identification.

claims.claim: If two face-colour classes each consist of exactly three hexagons together with any number of quadrilaterals, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: For their bichromatic graph H, the skeleton U has three degree-three vertices on each side. If H lacked a CAI-partition, claim 7 would force U-v to contain a cycle for every vertex v. The persisted checker exhaustively tested all 512 3-by-3 binary adjacency matrices and found exactly ten satisfying this condition: K3,3 and its nine one-edge deletions. K3,3 cannot occur in planar H. For K3,3 minus xy, the four non-endpoints already use all three incidences, while x and y have exactly one unused incidence each. The remaining maximal degree-2 path must join x to y, making H a subdivision of K3,3, again contradicting planarity. Thus H has a CAI-partition and claim 3 proves Hamiltonicity.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact enumeration of 512 matrices followed by analytic cubic-degree and planarity arguments.

claims.claim: Every graph satisfying the target assumptions with at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian; consequently these arguments force every counterexample to have at least 32 vertices.
claims.evidence: Writing n=2m, the exact identities are 2qi+3ri+si=m for each colour, q+r=m+2, hence r+s=m-4 and ri+si congruent to m modulo 2. Claim 8 gives ri>=3 in a counterexample. The persisted integer checker exhaustively enumerated all necessary profiles for 2<=m<=15: none occur for m<=12 or m=14; the sole m=13 profile and all nine m=15 profiles have at least two classes with (ri,si)=(3,0). Those classes consist of exactly three hexagons and quadrilaterals, so claim 9 applies. Thus every order at most 30 is covered. Cubicity forces even order, making 32 the next possible order.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact-integer face-profile enumeration plus the structural criterion in claim 9.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every graph satisfying the four assumptions is Hamiltonian or one explicit qualifying non-Hamiltonian graph with a rigorous certificate. The draft expressly says that it supplies neither, so it does not fully resolve the target and does not overclaim full coverage. Its verified results are nevertheless material: several sufficient conditions, a universal bounded-cycle 2-factor, structural restrictions on counterexamples, and a proof through 30 vertices. Accordingly the target verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. Because the draft labels its own resolution as PARTIAL, claimed_resolution is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
